title: PepperGate legal automation - customer call scratchbook
content:
Context:
- Intro call with PepperGate (legal document automation startup). They run a hosted SaaS for mid-market law firms to generate first-draft NDAs, engagement letters, and simple contract language.
- Concern: PII + client-confidential contract clauses must never be persisted in HW/cloud logs. Compliance team is very cautious — want private deployment in a VPC or on-premish setup.
- Tech contact: Amir Z., Head of Platform (callsigns: AZ). Product: Celia, Head of Ops.

High-level requirements (what they said on the call):
- Private control plane or private deployment behind their VPC — cannot send raw contracts to multi-tenant hosted inference.
- Hard SLOs: 300ms median for short prompts (<= 256 tokens), 95th <= 800ms for draft generation. Burst to 50 req/s sustained for 60s.
- Throughput: ~12k generated drafts/month, avg tokens per draft 900 (mostly initial generation + 1-2 rewrites).
- Retention: legal/regulatory — logs must be purged within 24 hours by default, configurable to 0 retention.
- Encryption + KMS/HSM integration: they use AWS KMS and want key ownership or HSM-backed envelope keys.
- Audit trail: every generation must be auditable, with anonymized prompt snapshots for quality monitoring (only metadata unless explicitly allowed).
- Model fidelity: prefer open models due to license and reproducibility. Will consider quantized 7B/13B models if legal style/quality acceptable.

Immediate gotchas & red flags (notes to self):
- They repeatedly emphasised "no egress; no implicit logging." That likely rules out Redwood Hosted API unless we run dedicated/private in their VPC or set up a strictly isolated private deployment.
- Data classification: they will mix PII (names, addresses) with legal clauses — must ensure prefix/KV caches never persist full documents beyond retention. Need explicit config option to disable caching or to use ephemeral-only caches for this customer.
- HSM integration: double-check our Private deployment HSM support — do we support AWS CloudHSM vs. external HSM vendors? If only KMS, that's an objection.
- Throughput/latency targets may force them toward smaller faster models or dedicated capacity with careful batching. Their prompt size (900 tokens avg) is non-trivial — memory/kv hit patterns matter.

Tech sketch / integration options (brain-dump):
1) Private (VPC) deployment: recommended. Install Redwood private control plane in their account or cross-account peering; inference nodes in their VPC, KMS keys in their account, no external egress.
   - Pros: meets "no-hosted-logs", BYOK, network isolation.
   - Cons: longer lead time, infra ops by PepperGate or co-managed.
2) Dedicated (reserved) but with strict egress controls: possible if we can guarantee zero-logging and bring-your-own-key via secure tunnel — probably still riskier than VPC option.
3) Hosted w/contractual: not acceptable to them.

Model and runtime considerations:
- Models to evaluate: Llama-2-13B/13B-chat, Mistral-instruct-7B, RedPine-7B (internal codenames). Need to run small evals for legal clause precision.
- Suggest experimenting with 13B quantized int8 + early-KV flush config to reduce hallucination on clause boundaries.
- For latency SLOs: set batch windows small (10-20ms) or disable batching for critical routes. But that increases cost. Consider dynamic policy: low-latency route uses dedicated pool with small batches, fallback to bulk pool for non-interactive workloads (batch quicker).
- Caching: prefix caching for standard boilerplate is beneficial, but for legal docs caching might leak. Offer a per-customer toggle: caching=off or cache-only-hashes (store only prompts hashes, not raw text).

Security & compliance items to confirm (actionable asks):
- Exact KMS/HSM vendor and whether they can provide a test key for integration.
- Contractual language for data retention and SOC2/ISO proofs. Supply necessary artifacts (SOC2 Type II report, penetration test summaries).
- Acceptable logging metadata: they said "we can allow tokens counts, latency, and model version info" but no prompt text. Confirm what anonymized telemetry shape is acceptable.
- Incident response SLA and contact list — they want a 24/7 escalation for suspected data leaks.

Prompt/wiring examples (quick prototypes to send):
- Prompt pattern (legal draft):
  "System: You are a legal-drafting assistant. Output must be in plain markdown and only include the requested clause(s). Do not add commentary.
  User: Draft a one-paragraph mutual NDA clause for US law, include clear definition of Confidential Information, term 3 years, and carve out for pre-existing knowledge.
  >>> Expected: Bullet/numbered clause + defined terms. No client name placeholders included; use <CLIENT_NAME> tag."
- Placeholder handling: propose convention using tags <CLIENT_NAME> etc. Important for traceability and to avoid storing live PII in logs (we can store HMAC'ed placeholders).

Next steps / immediate action items (owner initials):
- [Maya] Draft a short technical note that outlines VPC private deployment steps and time estimate (2–3 weeks for baseline deploy + readiness). Due: 2026-03-16.
- [Liam] Validate HSM compatibility matrix with infra team (does our private package support CloudHSM & vendor HSMs?). Due: 2026-03-14.
- [Priya] Prep SOC2 Type II and retention policy docs to send to PepperGate Legal. Due: 2026-03-13.
- [Maya + Amir] Schedule deep technical session — 60–90m — to walk through VPC architecture and run a small sample inference with dummy redacted docs. Target week of 03/23.
- Create a short eval: run Llama-2-13B and Mistral-7B on internal infra with 10 representative prompts from their sample (we have sample set they emailed). Compare: BLEU-like edit distance vs. their gold clauses + latency P95. (Owner: Maya).
- Add ticket to ENG backlog for per-customer cache policy toggle (JIRA-PG-1172).

Notes / color / conversational scraps: 
- Celia seemed pragmatic: will likely accept a Private VPC deploy if we give a clean onboarding checklist and a small POC to demonstrate redaction/retention guarantees.
- Amir is skeptical about BYOK latency tradeoffs — must include clear notes around KMS calls latency and caching of decrypted keys in enclave vs. calling KMS for every request.
- They asked about offline/on-prem appliance option — flag to product: is an air-gapped appliance feasible? (Probably >6 months dev cycle).

Random thoughts for sales deck later: emphasize "no-logs private inference with configurable retention + KMS BYOK" and show a simple architecture diagram: customer VPC -> private control plane -> inference pool (pinned nodes) -> HSM/KMS.

Meeting artifacts to attach to the customer:
- Short checklist: network peering steps, IAM role required, KMS key policy sample, sample redaction placeholder mapping.
- Quick eval table: model, expected latency (p50/p95), qualitative: clause precision.
- Next meeting proposal with time slots (03/23–03/25).

End-of-scratchpad — keep this messy. Will tidy into a proper one-pager after technical session and eval results.
